design_rationale: Participants were individually randomly assigned (1:1) to either dihydroartemisinin-piperaquine or placebo using central block randomisation stratified by country.

domain_judgments.rationale: Double-blind placebo-controlled design with identical packaging and high adherence (>90%), analysed using an appropriate intention-to-treat framework without substantial protocol deviations affecting assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Study drug tablets (dihydroartemisinin–piperaquine and placebo) were identically packaged. All study personnel, investigators, outcome assessors, data analysts, and participants remained masked to treatment assignment throughout the trial.

domain_judgments.rationale: Primary outcome data were available for 90% of randomized participants with similar retention between arms (89% vs 92%) and reasons for loss balanced and unrelated to the intervention.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Peripheral blood samples were collected at delivery from 602 (90%) of 666 participants, thus contributing to the primary endpoint analysis; of those, 294 women were in the intervention group and 308 women were in the control group.

domain_judgments.rationale: Standard objective laboratory measurement methods were utilized and outcome assessors were fully masked to intervention allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All study personnel, investigators, outcome assessors, data analysts, and participants remained masked to treatment assignment throughout the trial. domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a published protocol, prespecified primary and secondary outcomes were fully reported according to the analysis plan, and post-hoc analyses were clearly distinguished.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The trial protocol has been published elsewhere... This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT03671109... overall_summary: This was a well-conducted, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized trial with centralized concealed allocation, high participant adherence and retention, blinded outcome assessment, and protocol-consistent reporting, resulting in low risk of bias across all RoB 2 domains.

design_rationale: The study is a double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled trial where participants were randomly assigned (1:1) using permuted variable-sized blocks.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Women were randomly assigned to receive standard chemoprevention with daily TMP-SMX plus monthly placebo or daily TMP-SMX plus monthly DP in a 1:1 ratio, using permuted variable-sized blocks of 4 and 6. domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blinded with identical placebos, deviations from intended interventions were minimal, and analyses followed an intention-to-treat approach.

domain_judgments.rationale: All 200 enrolled women completed follow-up through delivery, and primary outcome data were available for 97% of participants (194/200), with very few balanced missing cases.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All 200 women enrolled were followed through delivery, and 194 (97%) had placental tissue collected for histopathologic analysis (Figure 1).

domain_judgments.rationale: Objective histopathologic and laboratory assessments were performed by outcome assessors who were blinded to treatment assignment.

R.), and any discrepant results were resolved by a third reader (A. M.). Readers were blinded to both treatment assignment and findings of prior reads.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was registered prospectively (NCT02282293) and all pre-specified outcomes and analyses are reported consistent with the protocol.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Clinical Trials Registration. NCT02282293. ... The primary outcome was detection of active or past placental malarial infection by histopathologic analysis. Secondary outcomes included incidence of malaria, parasite prevalence, and adverse birth outcomes.

overall_summary: The study is a well-conducted, double-blind, randomized placebo-controlled trial with central allocation concealment, high follow-up rate (97%), blinded outcome assessments, and pre-registered outcomes. All five RoB 2 domains were assessed as low risk of bias.

design_rationale: Participants were randomly assigned using a centralized computer-generated block randomization list stratified by country with allocation concealment via opaque sealed envelopes.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind with identical placebo tablets, blinding was maintained, and appropriate ITT analyses were performed without notable protocol deviations.

domain_judgments.evidence_quote: A total of 973 peripheral blood samples from women at delivery were collected (490 from control and 483 from MQ group).

overall_summary: This was a rigorously designed, double-blind, multicenter randomized placebo-controlled trial with central randomization, effective blinding, low and balanced attrition, standardized objective outcome measurements, and adherence to a pre-specified protocol and analysis plan. design_rationale: The study is an individually randomised, two-arm, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial where participants were randomly assigned (1:1) by computer-generated block randomisation.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was computer-generated, concealed via sequentially numbered sealed opaque envelopes prepared by independent personnel, and baseline characteristics were well-balanced between groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was double-blind and placebo-controlled with identical-appearing tablets, and analyses were conducted according to an intention-to-treat approach without substantial deviations.

domain_judgments.rationale: Outcome data were available for 99% of enrolled participants, with missing data balanced across groups and sensitivity analyses confirming the robustness of the results.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: Of Nov 11, 2019, to Aug 3, 2021, 904 women were enrolled and randomly assigned... of whom 895 (99%) contributed to the primary analysis... The proportion of eligible participants with missing primary endpoint data was equally distributed across study groups.

domain_judgments.rationale: The outcome was assessed using objective diagnostic tests (PCR, microscopy, rapid tests, histology) and outcome assessors and laboratory staff were masked to treatment assignment.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary endpoint was the incidence of Plasmodium infection detected in the peripheral (maternal) or placental (maternal) blood or tissue by PCR, microscopy, rapid diagnostic test, or placental histology... domain_judgments.rationale: The trial was prospectively registered with a prespecified statistical analysis plan, and reported results aligned with prespecified outcomes and analyses.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: All analyses were prespecified (unless otherwise indicated as post hoc) in a statistical analysis plan approved by the data and safety monitoring board... This trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04158713.

overall_summary: This is a well-conducted, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized clinical trial with low risk of bias across all five RoB 2 domains. The overall risk of bias is low.

design_rationale: The study is described as two randomized controlled trials, with participants randomly allocated to treatment groups via stratified randomization managed by a central coordination center by phone.

domain_judgments.rationale: The allocation sequence was stratified and centrally controlled with treatment assignments provided by phone, ensuring adequate sequence generation and allocation concealment, and baseline characteristics were well balanced between groups.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: In each trial, randomization was stratified according to the study site and the number of previous pregnancies (primigravid vs. multigravid). The study coordination center retained the master list and assigned treatments by phone.

domain_judgments.rationale: Although the trial was open-label, deviations from intended interventions were low, adherence was closely monitored, and both modified intention-to-treat and per-protocol analyses yielded consistent findings.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: We designed 2 parallel open-label, noninferiority controlled trials... This trial was blinded only to the microscopists who evaluated blood smears.

domain_judgments.rationale: Approximately 20% to 23% of participants in each trial were missing the primary outcome (placental blood collection at delivery), and while proportions were similar across arms, those with missing data differed systematically regarding timing of HIV diagnosis, raising some concerns for bias due to missing data.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: 108 (77%) and 233 (80%), respectively, had the primary end point assessed. The proportions of women not included in the mITT population were similar in different trials and treatment groups (Fig. 1). Overall, women with missing primary end point had been more frequently diagnosed for HIV during the ongoing pregnancy (56% vs. 38%, P = 0.003), and their HIV diagnosis was more recent (2.4 vs. 19.0 months ago in median, P = 0.005).

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary outcome was assessed using objective microscopic analysis and PCR by independent microscopists who were masked to treatment allocation.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: This trial was blinded only to the microscopists who evaluated blood smears... For malaria diagnosis, thick and thin blood smears were stained with Giemsa and read by 2 independent microscopists, with conciliation of discrepancies by a third reader.

domain_judgments.rationale: The primary and secondary outcomes were analyzed according to a pre-specified statistical analysis plan and reported comprehensively with transparent notation of a protocol amendment for PCR outcomes.
domain_judgments.evidence_quote: The primary end point was the prevalence of placental parasitemia assessed by microscopy. Secondary end points were incident parasitemia during follow-up, the prevalence of peripheral parasitemia at delivery, the mean birth weight, and proportion of low birth weight infants... Malarial infections detected by PCR in placental and peripheral blood at delivery were added as secondary end points after a protocol amendment.

overall_summary: The overall risk of bias is rated as some concerns, driven primarily by Domain 3 due to missing primary outcome data in 20% to 23% of randomized participants and baseline differences in HIV diagnosis timing between those with and without complete outcome data. Other domains demonstrated low risk of bias with centralized randomization, masked outcome assessors for parasitology, and pre-specified analyses.
